source.title: Embryology of a Language Model
source.authors: George Wang; Garrett Baker; Andrew Gordon; Daniel Murfet

page_placements.theme: Developmental signatures of induction-circuit formation (LLC, susceptibilities, influence functions, spectra)

record.tranche_reason: Uses susceptibility patterns and their UMAP/PCA structure to examine induction-circuit development, rather than the original prefix-score and in-context-learning measurements. It also compares the development across four training seeds.
record.gate_note: The paper measures induction-pattern susceptibilities and their organization in susceptibility space over training. Its references to prefix scores, ICL scores, and K-composition results from earlier work are cited background, not results of this study. It does not measure later-token loss relative to earlier tokens, a loss-curve bump, few-shot task learning, or behavior across different model families, sizes, or data setups.
record.test_reason: This is a methods paper on UMAP of per-token susceptibilities. It takes the induction circuit (heads 0:1, 0:4, 0:5, 1:6, 1:7) and stages LM3–LM4 from earlier work (Hoogland et al., Wang et al.) as ground truth. It then shows its own susceptibility visualisation recovers them, which the authors say 'validates our approach'. It measures susceptibility (a loss-landscape covariance), not induction behaviour: no prefix scores, copying, composition, ICL score, or loss-curve timing are measured here. Its findings are recorded under fits_no_version, not as tests of V1–V7.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. Add that the authors present the visible emergence of the induction circuit as validation of their method. Their headline novel finding is a 'spacing fin' structure that counts spacing tokens. Seed universality refers to the high-level body plan; the specific heads doing induction differ across seeds.
record.recipe_differences: Uses per-token susceptibilities, PCA, and UMAP to track pattern organization and development; does not reproduce the original prefix-score plus ICL-score measurement. This is an empirical extension of susceptibility-based structural inference.
record.method_sensitivity: UMAP figures use n_neighbors=45 and min_dist=0.1; the authors report checking n_neighbors from 15 to the equivalent of 8000 and min_dist from 0 to 0.5, with no substantial differences in the plots for different min_dist values. Stage boundaries differ by small amounts across seeds.

fits_no_version.finding: Induction-pattern susceptibilities in both layers are small and negative until about 2000 steps, then rise slowly, then rapidly before 10000 steps. In seed 1, PC2 variance for induction tokens rises from 2.3% to 6.4% between steps 9000 and 17500.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Susceptibility signatures of the induction circuit change gradually from about 2k steps, then sharply during LM3–LM4.

fits_no_version.finding: PCA of susceptibilities across both layers places the previously identified previous-token, current-token and induction heads at the extremes of the loadings. This holds in all four seeds, even though which specific heads do induction differs by seed.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Structural inference via susceptibilities recovers the known induction circuit across seeds.

record.problems: The study examines only a 3M-parameter, two-layer attention-only transformer and four seeds in one training setting. It relies on UMAP, which the authors note can distort global distances, and it does not directly test copy behavior, causal composition, ICL, or loss-curve timing.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant results left out. Spacing-fin results and other token-pattern analyses are not rows because they do not measure the listed claim versions.

untested.parts: No composition, attention-pattern or copying measurement; induction heads are taken from prior work.
No prefix score, ICL score, or loss-curve bump timing measured.
No in-context learning or large models.
Induction heads per seed come from prior work; no other families, sizes, architectures or modalities.
Training data and setup are not varied.
Formation sub-steps are not measured here; the K-composition and prefix-score timing are cited from prior work.

record.verdict_notes: The reader treated this as a T2 test. But the study's induction-related results are susceptibility and visualisation outputs, checked against induction heads and stage boundaries established by Hoogland et al. and Wang et al. The prefix-score, ICL-score and K-composition timings appear only as cited comparisons.

versions.untested_parts: Does not directly test K-composition or causally verify that the heads copy [B] in the [A][B] … [A] → [B] task; its evidence is susceptibility-based association with induction patterns and previously identified heads.
Measures induction-related development, but not the timing of an ICL gain, later-token loss falling relative to earlier tokens, or a training-loss bump.
Does not test most in-context learning in large transformers or measure loss falling with token index.
Tests four seeds of the same 3M-parameter, two-layer attention-only transformer in the same training setting, not other model families, sizes, architectures, or modalities.
Does not vary training data or setup to test their effects on induction formation or persistent in-context learning.
Does not evaluate few-shot task learning or compare induction heads with other mechanisms as carriers of it.
Tracks susceptibility and visualization changes for induction patterns, but does not independently test all proposed circuit substeps or quantify their causal contributions.

rows.subject: seed 1 3M parameter attention-only transformer
rows.operation_detail: Examined PCA loadings of the combined-layer susceptibility data matrix on attention heads.

conditions.value: induction patterns and other token patterns

rows.measure: Head loadings on principal components of susceptibility data
rows.value: Loadings are broadly positive in layer 0 and negative in layer 1; layer 0 previous-token and current-token heads have the highest magnitude, while layer 1 induction heads have the lowest (most positive) magnitude.
rows.note: This is structural association in susceptibility space, not a direct composition or causal copying test.
rows.check: PCA head loadings show the method aligns with heads already identified as the induction circuit by prior work. This is method validation and does not test K-composition or [A][B]…[A]→[B] copying.

rows.operation_detail: Compared head loadings in PCA of the susceptibility data across training seeds.

conditions.value: same architecture and training distribution as seed 1

rows.measure: Head loadings on principal components of susceptibility data
rows.value: The combined-layer loading pattern described for seed 1 also holds in the other three seeds.
rows.note: The paper reports the same qualitative loading pattern across the other three seeds; no numerical loading values are stated in the text.
rows.check: Across seeds, the induction heads are taken from Wang et al. and differ by seed (seed 2: 1:0; seed 3: 1:6; seed 4: 1:1, 1:3). The row shows the method's loading pattern recurs, not that induction heads form, so it does not test V1 or V4 here.

rows.subject: seed 1 3M parameter attention-only transformer
rows.operation_detail: Visualized susceptibility vectors with UMAP and compared induction-pattern separation over training.
rows.baseline: At 9000 steps, no dorsal-ventral stratification by token color is visible.
rows.value: At 17500 steps, dorsal-ventral stratification is obvious.
rows.note: The authors describe the change as visible by the end of LM4; UMAP is a visualization rather than a direct behavioral measure.
rows.check: UMAP dorsal-ventral stratification is a visualisation of susceptibility space. It is not a measure of induction behaviour, ICL, or loss-bump timing.

rows.check: The 'universality' here concerns the susceptibility body plan across seeds of one model and training setup. It is not the presence of induction heads measured by this study.

relation.reason: Section 4.2 attributes prefix scores, ICL scores, K-composition, and circuit identities to earlier work. The present study visualizes their correspondence with susceptibility structure; the conclusion explicitly treats recovery of the known induction circuit as validation of its method.

tranche.reason: The study uses previously identified induction heads and developmental stages to validate susceptibility visualization. Its new measurements concern susceptibility geometry, rather than copying behavior, composition, or coincident changes in ICL and loss.

source_check.notes: The PC2 percentages concern variance within the induction-token subset. Similarity across seeds concerns susceptibility organization; specific induction-head identities differ across seeds.
